conflicts.subject: model
conflicts.detail: Authorization models differ (A: budget membership: members see a budget's expenses; owner manages members; B: none (single-user library function))
solutions: Choose one authorization model and express the others' rules in it
conflicts.recommended: One authorization model with one permission check function

resolution.decision: One model: budget membership with roles owner and member. Every expense belongs to a budget; each user gets a personal budget at sign-up (Spendly's single-user use). One can_access(user, action, record) function used by every route and query.

conflicts.subject: conversion-target-currency
conflicts.detail: Tallyho converts foreign receipts to the user's home currency (documented), but its shared budget totals are in one budget currency (screenshot: EUR). Members of one budget can have different home currencies, so 'home currency' totals would disagree between members. Spendly records no currency at all.
solutions: Convert to the budget's currency for the expense and its totals; keep the original amount and currency
Convert to each viewer's home currency at display time
No conversion: reject expenses not in the budget currency
conflicts.recommended: Convert to the budget's currency, store original amount, currency, rate and rate date; every member sees the same totals

resolution.decision: Convert to the budget's currency. Store original amount and currency, converted amount in budget currency, rate and rate date (receipt date). Totals use the converted amount; every member sees the same totals.

conflicts.subject: access-after-member-removal
conflicts.detail: Tallyho documents that the owner can remove members, and the user saw that a removed member's earlier expenses stay in the budget; whether the removed member can still see the budget is not known. Left unclear, a removed person might keep seeing everyone's spending.
solutions: Keep their expenses in the budget, end their access at once
Delete or move their expenses out of the budget on removal
Let them keep read access to their own past expenses
conflicts.recommended: Keep their expenses (totals stay correct, as in Tallyho) and end all their access to the budget at once

resolution.decision: On removal, the member loses all access to the budget immediately; their earlier expenses stay in the budget, attributed to them, and keep counting in totals. Only the owner may remove; the owner cannot remove themself.

conflicts.subject: session
conflicts.detail: Session mechanisms differ (A: unknown for the app; bearer token in the authorization header for the api; B: none)
solutions: Choose one session mechanism (http-only cookie sessions are the safer default for web apps)
Use tokens only where a client cannot hold cookies
conflicts.recommended: One session mechanism for the whole app

resolution.decision: Server-side sessions in http-only, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookies for the web app. Tallyho's personal access tokens are not built (M11 deferred).

conflicts.subject: tenancy
conflicts.detail: tenant boundaries differ (A: budget (inferred), B: none)
solutions: Choose one tenant boundary (organisation, workspace...) and assign every row to a tenant
Keep single-tenant data in one default tenant, decided with the user
conflicts.recommended: One tenant model; every tenant-owned row has a tenant key and every query filters by it

resolution.decision: The budget is the tenant boundary: Expense, BudgetMember and Invitation carry budget_id and every query filters by the caller's memberships. Nothing is shared across budgets.

conflicts.subject: scanned-expense-category
conflicts.detail: Tallyho's scan fills merchant, date and total but no category is documented; Spendly rejects any expense without a known category. A scanned receipt would either fail to save or need a silent default.
solutions: Require the user to pick a category on the review screen before saving
Default scanned expenses to 'other'
Guess a category from the merchant
conflicts.recommended: Require a category on the review screen (no silent default); Spendly's rule stays intact

resolution.decision: Category is required on the scan review screen; no silent default; Spendly's reject-unknown rule applies to scanned expenses too.

conflicts.subject: expense
conflicts.detail: Expense may not mean the same thing in A, B: A describes it as 'A spending record in a budget, as exposed by the public API', B as 'A spending record: amount in cents, a category, an optional note'
solutions: Keep them as separate entities with distinct names (for example UserAccount and LedgerAccount)
Merge them only if the user confirms they describe the same thing
conflicts.recommended: Ask the user; never merge entities because their names match

resolution.decision: Same concept in both (one spending record). One Expense entity: Tallyho's merchant, currency, date, budget plus Spendly's integer amount, category and note.

conflicts.subject: expense.amount
conflicts.detail: Expense.amount types differ (A: number, B: integer)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: amount_minor: integer (bigint) minor units. Decimal user input such as 12.40 is parsed to 1240 using the currency's exponent; zero and negative rejected.

conflicts.subject: expense.amount.unit
conflicts.detail: Expense.amount unit differs (A: major units, B: minor units (cents))
solutions: Store one unit (for example integer cents in UTC) and convert at import
Store the unit with the value
conflicts.recommended: One unit per field, converted in the migration and tested

resolution.decision: Minor units everywhere (Spendly's unit), with an ISO 4217 currency on every amount; display formats to major units.

conflicts.subject: monthly-reset-meaning
conflicts.detail: 'Budgets reset monthly' does not say what resets, on which day or in which time zone.
solutions: Calendar-month period in the budget's time zone; spent counts expenses dated in it; nothing deleted
Rolling 30-day window
Archive expenses at month end
conflicts.recommended: Calendar-month period in the budget's time zone, by expense date; nothing deleted

resolution.decision: Budget period is the calendar month in the budget's time zone; spent vs limit counts expenses dated in that month; nothing is deleted; past months stay viewable. To confirm with the user.

conflicts.subject: expense-currency-missing-in-b
conflicts.detail: Spendly expenses have no currency or date; Tallyho expenses need both.
solutions: Currency defaults to the budget currency and date to today when not given
Make both required on every entry
conflicts.recommended: Default currency to the budget currency and date to today in the entry form; both stored as required columns

resolution.decision: currency and date are required columns; the entry form defaults currency to the budget currency and date to today.

conflicts.subject: expense
conflicts.detail: deleting a Expense means different things (A: hard delete (no marker found), B: hard)
solutions: Choose soft or hard delete for the merged entity and convert the other source's rows
Keep deleted rows from the soft-delete source as archived
conflicts.recommended: Soft delete for merged data unless the user decides otherwise

resolution.decision: Hard delete, allowed to the member who added the expense or the budget owner (Tallyho's delete behaviour is unknown; Spendly has none).

conflicts.subject: expense
conflicts.detail: Expense exists in A:Expense, B:Expense; fields not shared: budget_id (only A), currency (only A), date (only A), merchant (only A), note (only B)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge only once it is confirmed they mean the same thing; then list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merged into one Expense entity (see entity-meaning).

conflicts.subject: expense.primary-key
conflicts.detail: Expense primary key type is not known for A, B; find it before deciding the merged key
solutions: Read the source's schema or migrations for the type
Record it as unknown and decide in the architecture
conflicts.recommended: Find the real type before designing the merged entity

resolution.decision: New uuid primary key; neither source's key is carried over (no data is migrated).
